departments.headline: WORKING FROM THE ZONE
departments.dek: Most commanders must resolve to matter. Yours bills the table from the command zone all game — and the record shows the discount, the tax, and the rental clause all favor rarely casting him at all.
departments.body:
Start with what the zone guarantees: your commander is always available to cast from the command zone (CR 903.4). This deck files that guarantee differently from every other list at the table. The Ur-Dragon's eminence ability works while he sits in the zone — every Dragon spell you cast costs {1} less, from turn zero, for as long as the game lasts. The guarantee is not that you will draw him. It is that you are always being paid.

Now the tax. Each cast from the zone after the first costs an additional {2} (CR 903.8). The ladder reads nine, eleven, thirteen — against a deck whose mean available mana on turn nine is 6.165. The record is blunt: the first cast is an event, the second is a stretch, the third is fiction. Protection is therefore the better spend, and the deck's own insurance argues the same — Deflecting Swat is free only while a commander is on your battlefield, so landing him once and keeping him is worth more than any recast plan.

There is a rental clause, and the Counselor commends it to your attention. Hellkite Courser's enters-trigger puts The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, hasty, for exactly one attack — a card per attacking Dragon plus a free permanent from hand — then returns him at end step. The tax counts casts (CR 903.8), and this never was one. The zone gets its tenant back untaxed. The route everyone assumes works, Sneak Attack, does not: it reaches creature cards in your hand, and the command zone is not your hand (CR 903.6; the full holding is case A-005).

Color identity: five colours costs you nothing in exclusions — every card in the format's identity rules is available to this list — and everything in logistics. The 99 pays for WUBRG with sixteen tapped lands and an eleven-source black column; Sources Say prices that bill in full.

The 21-point clock (CR 903.10a) is arithmetic worth savoring: a 10/10 commander deals 20 commander damage in two connections — one point short. Three clean hits close it, and a Thrakkus the Butcher doubling still stops at 20 on one swing. The holding: commander damage here is a coincidence, not a plan. The deck's real kills are filed under The Kill.

The Coach's close: cast him when the table's interaction is spent, shield him once he lands, and never mulligan a hand looking for him. The zone already holds him — and the zone is where he earns.

captions.Hellkite Courser: **THE RENTAL CLAUSE:** his enters-trigger borrows The Ur-Dragon from the command zone with haste for one attack — a draw per attacking Dragon plus a free permanent, returned untaxed at end step.

pilot_tips.text: Save Teferi's Protection for the turn The Ur-Dragon finally lands — a nine-mana body with no shield is the most expensive way to donate a wrath.

departments.headline: LET THEM WATCH THE WRONG CLOCK
departments.dek: The table budgets its answers for a nine-mana commander who averages a turn-8.967 arrival. Your actual clock is one enchantment and a connecting Dragon — and the checker already signed off on it.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Korlessa, Scale Singer early and play Dragons off the top — with eminence discounting every Dragon spell from the command zone, your library is a second hand.

captions.Aggravated Assault: **THE REAL CLOCK:** every contained infinite in this deck routes through this one enchantment — it comes down the turn it wins, never a turn before.
captions.The Ur-Dragon: **THE DECOY:** mean cast turn 8.967, 0.0% by turn six — eminence does his work from the command zone while the table watches the wrong threat.

departments.pull_quote: Nobody watching for The Ur-Dragon is watching the actual clock.

departments.headline: NINETY-NINE SEATS, RANKED
departments.dek: The engine room first — eleven cards the checker already put on the record — then the payoffs, the discounts, the wallet, and a mana base carrying five colours' worth of bills.

roster.role: The engine room — on the record

captions.Atsushi, the Blazing Sky: **THE WALKING BANK:** his death mints three unrestricted Treasures — exactly the mana the spells-only sources can never provide for Aggravated Assault.

pilot_tips.text: Cast your whole hand with Klauth's attack mana — but never budget it for Aggravated Assault: it pays for spells only, and an activated ability is not a spell.

departments.pull_quote: Every sleeve either feeds the threshold or funds the exit.

departments.headline: MULLIGAN FOR FUNCTION
departments.dek: The simulation keeps 75.1% of opening sevens, so your gut is usually right. Call these four out loud, then check the receipts — a cost reducer reaches your hand by turn six in only 33.2% of games, and it is the keep that matters.

hands.why: A cost reducer plus Sol Ring is the hand the deck is thirsting for: reducers show by turn six in just 33.2% of games, and they — not land drops — compress a nine-drop curve into a castable one.
The payoff layer pays per Dragon and wants to be down before the first one lands. A payoff is drawn by turn six in 62.2% of games; this hand starts one on turn two.

hands.verdict: KEEP — the loud card, held quietly
hands.why: Assault in the opener is a hold, not a keep-reason — it wins with a board and funding, and it is the deck's loudest tell. The keep is the ramp, the engine half, and Atsushi's three unrestricted Treasures.
Two lands and five cards costing five-plus, no bridge between them. Mean available mana on turn six is 4.937 — this hand starts working around turn eight, and the game will not wait.

pilot_tips.text: Keep almost any seven holding Urza's Incubator — with eminence it takes {3} off every Dragon, and the simulation says you will not see another reducer soon.

departments.pull_quote: You never mulligan for the commander — the command zone already holds him.

departments.headline: COMMIT BEFORE YOU PEEK
departments.dek: Two real boards from this exact 99: a castable commander staring down five untapped control lands, and a Tiamat pile you must design into telegraphed sweeper mana. Decide out loud first — the Coach shows his hand after you show yours.
departments.pull_quote: A good read costs nothing. A bad commit costs the game.
departments.note: Render decisions 001 then 002. Recommendations stay below the branches per STYLEv3 section 5.1 — no caption, callout, or dek may telegraph either answer.

departments.headline: SIX VERDICTS, ONE PAYROLL
departments.dek: Two true infinites, a d20 burst, a doubling audit, a sweeper turned execution, and a famous cheat denied in court. Every line below survived the adversarial checker — nothing here is hope.

callouts.title: THE SWING
callouts.text: Old Gnawbone connects for 7. Treasures equal to combat damage dealt to players — seven tokens hit the table (stack 006).

callouts.title: THE PAYMENT
callouts.text: Five Treasures pay Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R}. Untap your creatures; take another combat phase.

callouts.title: THE MARGIN
callouts.text: Each cycle banks net +2 Treasures. The moment nothing can block a 7/7 flier, the engine is unbounded.

callouts.title: THE EXECUTIONS
callouts.text: Opponents fall sequentially — the first on combat 6, the second on combat 12 of the verified game.

callouts.title: THE ACCOUNTING
callouts.text: You end with exactly 22 Treasures, not 29: the game ends by state-based action before Gnawbone's final trigger ever reaches the stack.

captions.Savage Ventmaw: **THE SELF-FUNDING LOOP:** attack mana pays the reactivation with {R} to spare — +1 per cycle, and the trigger fires on declaration, before blockers matter (stack 003).
captions.Sneak Attack: **THE REFUTATION:** it cheats any Dragon in the 99 into play for {R} — and it cannot touch The Ur-Dragon, because the command zone is not your hand (stack 005).
captions.Wrathful Red Dragon: **THE HONEST LIMIT:** 39 redirected damage executes one opponent at 39 or less life, never the table — and destroy-all wraths feed it nothing (stack 004).

pilot_tips.text: Protect Aggravated Assault like the win condition it is — every infinite in this docket routes through it, and no second extra-combat effect is sleeved.

departments.pull_quote: The database alleges; the checker adjudicates.
departments.note: Feature spread order: 006 (the cover line, walked in the callout-steps), 003, 001, 002, 004, 005. Dossier pointers to cases A-001 through A-006 are renderer-standing.

departments.headline: THE SLOWEST DECK IN THE ROOM
departments.dek: Five-colour Dragons reads as battlecruiser, and your first four turns confirm the story. Keep it that way — your real tells are two enchantments, and bracket-4 tables answer them on sight.

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: You flip to archenemy the turn Aggravated Assault is live with a connecting Old Gnawbone or Savage Ventmaw — funding on the table, protection held. The shield is in hand by turn six in 66.0% of games. Choose that turn; never drift into it.

callouts.title: THE SECOND WINDOW
callouts.text: With Wrathful Red Dragon out, welcome the damage sweeper: stack 004 verified 39 redirected at one face. Quote it honestly at the table — it executes one player, never three, and destroy-all wraths feed it nothing.

captions.Sneak Attack: **THE TELL YOU CAN AFFORD:** an enchantment the wraths never touch — but the table prices {R} Drakuseths the moment it lands, so land it the turn it deals 17, not before.
captions.Dragonlord Dromoka: **THE QUIET COMMIT:** opponents cannot cast spells during your turn — sequence her first on the pivot turn, and everything after her resolves in peace.

pilot_tips.text: Hold Deflecting Swat for the removal spell aimed at Aggravated Assault mid-combo — never spend it saving a Signet's worth of value.

departments.pull_quote: Stay boring until the turn you aren't.

departments.headline: FOUR FIGHTS, NAMED OUTS
departments.dek: Sweepers, stax, aggro, and faster combo — each one beats you a different way, and every out below is actually sleeved in this 99.

threats.read: Your board is thin by design — 1.463 mean bodies at turn six — so waves cost you little, and your rebuild is enchantment-shaped: Assault, Sneak Attack, and the draw layer never die to a wrath. With Wrathful Red Dragon out, a damage sweeper is their mistake (stack 004). Destroy-all effects still trade clean — hold one shield for the board that actually wins.

Taxes punish a 23-card five-to-seven shelf, but eminence accrues from the command zone where permanent-hate cannot reach, Treasure bursts pay in lump sums, and the Ventmaw loop needs exactly one clean combat (stack 003). Aim your removal at whatever taxes untaps or activations — Assault is the whole exit.

You are the control seat: roughly 120 combined life stands behind three defenses, and your fliers blank ground boards. Crux of Fate spares every Dragon you own. Do not race — the long game belongs to your engine.

Spend answers at the win attempt, never earlier. The suite is real coverage — and you race credibly, since your own two-card lines assemble at six mana or less. In the counter-war, Dovin's Veto has the last word.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Crux of Fate as your one-sided wrath — all non-Dragons die, your whole board stays — and save Blasphemous Act for the turns Wrathful Red Dragon is watching.

departments.headline: FOUR ROADS, ONE CITY
departments.dek: Four tutors, thirteen wishes, and nearly every road leads to Aggravated Assault plus a connecting Dragon. Tiamat headlines: one resolved cast hands you a five-name package — both kill halves, the doubler, the haste anthem, and the commander's courier.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Enlightened Tutor at the end of the turn before you win — the reveal announces Aggravated Assault to the whole table, so buy it with Deflecting Swat held.

departments.pull_quote: A wish is also an announcement — shop the turn before, never two.

departments.headline: RED WRITES THE CHECKS
departments.dek: Red is 46.5% of the pip bill on 26.2% of the land sources. Black runs eleven lands against a double-black lump. Sixteen of twenty-nine lands arrive tapped. The audit prices all of it — and names the Treasury that never appears on the books.

captions.The World Tree: **THE SECOND LANTERN:** at six lands, every land you control taps for any colour — five separate shortfalls collapse into one solved number.

pilot_tips.text: Fetch the Swamp with Fabled Passage the turn before Patriarch's Bidding — black is the thinnest column at eleven land sources, and its eight pips arrive in double-black lumps.

departments.pull_quote: This deck doesn't miss colours so much as it misses tempo.

departments.headline: EIGHT POINT NINE SIX SEVEN
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded games put the commander on the stand: mean cast turn 8.967, 0.0% by turn six, cast at all by turn ten in just 13.7% of runs. That is not an indictment — it is the case for the engines.

callouts.title: EARLY MONEY
callouts.text: Ramp or fixing is drawn by turn six in 71.6% of games, mean arrival turn 2.588. The first act funds itself.

callouts.title: THE RARE FIXER
callouts.text: A cost reducer shows by turn six in just 33.2% of games — and the model does not even simulate the discount. When you hold one, build the turn around it.

callouts.title: THE FADE
callouts.text: Land drops decay to 49.7% by turn six while mean mana sits at 4.937 — from there the deck climbs on rocks, Treasures, and discounts.

callouts.title: THE SHIELD RATE
callouts.text: Protection is in hand by turn six in 66.0% of games. The plan asks for exactly one shielded turn; the ledger says you will usually have it.

captions.Urza's Incubator: **OFF THE BOOKS:** cost reducers go unmodeled, so 8.967 is the floor of the problem, not your ceiling.
captions.Old Gnawbone: **ALSO OFF THE BOOKS:** the model mints no Treasures — the deck's single richest income line is invisible to every number on this page.

pilot_tips.text: Play Mox Jasper the moment a Dragon hits your board — the mana table counts it from that turn on, and banking it early costs you nothing.

departments.pull_quote: The commander is an event. The engines are the schedule.

departments.headline: TEN SCOUTS, NO SPARES
departments.dek: This deck carries no sideboard, so all ten picks are scouted from the wider pool. Seven buy a second card name for the verified Assault architecture — led by Hellkite Charger and The Reaver Cleaver — because one enchantment currently carries all three infinites.

callouts.title: THE STANDING RULE
callouts.text: Every combo line a pick opens is a candidate — needs a stack scenario, pick by pick — and no pick moves the computed floor off 4. Buy the scenario before you lean a game on the line.

callouts.title: THE PILOT'S NAMES
callouts.text: Hellkite Tyrant and Faeburrow Elder appear in no evidence channel. Tyrant's theft line is live in Treasure pods but competes with picks that end games through the verified architecture; Faeburrow fights the deck's shape twice — ramp is over budget and {W} is the thinnest colour. Overriding the data is a pilot call; the ledger just prices it.

pilot_tips.text: If Three Visits earns a sleeve, cut Skyshroud Claim — the obsolescence trace reads similarity 0.9983 at two mana less, and the ramp budget is already the deck's fattest line.

departments.pull_quote: When one card carries three infinites, redundancy is the cheapest insurance on the market.

departments.headline: SIX CASES, VERBATIM
departments.dek: Every citation quoted in full, every verdict stamped after an adversarial second read. Case A-005 alone is worth the visit: the famous cheat, denied, with the rule that denies it.
departments.note: Cases A-001 through A-006 render from checker-passed stacks, citations untouched. A-006 backs the cover; A-005 carries the CR 903.6 refutation the teases sell.

departments.headline: A HOARD OF HANDS
departments.dek: No painter owns this deck: 76 artists across 95 cards, and the largest single hand is four. The ledger calls that breadth, not indecision — and it credits every hand per card, never per copy.

featured.note:
The hero seat goes to Jaime Jones, who painted the face of the franchise: The Ur-Dragon himself, plus Dragonlord Kolaghan's haste anthem and the Temur Ascendancy that turns your board into cards. Three cards — and honesty first: that is not even the deck's largest hand. Adam Paquette holds four, and every one of them is mana.

Read the counts for what they are: per card, never per copy — the four Mountains share one Jonas De Ro painting and count once. The 95 cards arrive from 41 different products, the largest cluster is eight cards from Tarkir: Dragonstorm Commander spread across eight different painters, and no collector-number run suggests a box bought whole. This collection was assembled the slow way, one Dragon at a time, and the ledger shows it: breadth all the way down, with exactly one foil in the stack.

also_worth_noting.note: Four cards, the deck's largest hand — Blood Crypt, Cinder Glade, Steam Vents, and Dragon's Hoard. The whole portfolio is infrastructure: the painter of the bills this deck pays.
Three, all load-bearing: Drakuseth, Maw of Flames — stack 005's star — plus Urza's Incubator and Rootbound Crag.
Two cards, both of them stack fights: Deflecting Swat and Dovin's Veto — a quarter of the counter-war from one hand.

captions.The Ur-Dragon: **THE FACE:** Jaime Jones' commander portrait — the one card the whole table prices, painted at hero scale.

departments.pull_quote: Breadth all the way down — one Dragon at a time.

rhythm_notes: The five-act flight plan does the pacing. Sunny opens in the cockpit — narrative thesis, hand drill, then the participation peak of two decision spreads. Act II cools into reflection (Table Manners), holds reference (Know Your Enemy) between two lighter instruction spreads, and closes on Fetch Quests. Act III hands the long game to Vera's Command Zone instruction, exhales through the roster's browsing, and lets Ledger's Short List run on imagination. Act IV climbs: Sources Say's dense audit breathes through the declared full-bleed art break (issue_spec.BREATHER_AFTER) into By the Numbers' second dense spread, then peaks at The Kill — the docket carries the issue's most ambitious layout, with the 006 payroll walked step by step. Act V parks Judge's Desk's opt-in density directly behind that narrative, cools through Featured Artist's appreciation, and exits on the Back Page. Pull quotes sit as micro-breathers on the seven longest sections; no two dense modes are adjacent anywhere without the declared breather between them.
gaps: Cavern-Hoard Dragon + Aggravated Assault is the one contained infinite with no stack — its Treasure funding depends on the defender's artifact count, so the scenario would bound it, not just bless it. Until then every department treats it as a candidate.

Two frame-flagged scenarios worth buying: Sneak Attack at instant speed cheating Wrathful Red Dragon in under a sweeper (would extend verified 004), and Miirym + Sneak Attack — does the token copy survive the end-step sacrifice?

Scourge of the Throne's dethrone recheck on later combats is an open rules question — The 99's tile carries the caution; a scenario would settle whether it is a second extra-combat engine or a one-shot.

Short List scenarios in priority order (from considering.json): The Reaver Cleaver + Assault Treasure accounting, Old Gnawbone + Hellkite Charger, Helm of the Host + Scourge of the Throne's dethrone condition.

Strategy DB holes the frame names and this issue felt: extra-combat chaining as a school, kill-order sequencing when a line kills sequentially (stack 006 does), cheat-into-play economics, and typal payoff density.
